account:
It is noon, and I am home for my scheduled lunch after the morning market walk. Town business seems fairly ordinary so far, though I have learned little concrete news. The builder approached me seeking this week's repair scope and payment, with planks and lanterns ready. I have no confirmed damage reports, so I asked for a specific proposal at my one o'clock accounts appointment and explicitly authorized neither work nor payment. The secretary can record any agreement.

The baker appears active supplying bread: townsfolk reported seeing the baker carrying wheat at the bakery and later bread near the inn. I personally saw the baker carrying a sack of bread at the market stall and putting bread into its chest. This looks consistent with baking and stocking the stall, not evidence of anything improper. I bought one fresh loaf for lunch. Freight was near town hall holding an emerald, but my attempts to speak were reported unheard, and I could not make out freight's speech; I cannot say what freight is doing beyond that observation.

My three o'clock tea remains an unresolved practical matter: the appointment book says only 'the neighbour, dockside cottage, east bank,' and the secretary did not know which cottage or neighbour. I should establish the host and location before the appointment. After lunch I must attend town accounts at one, tea at three, office at four-thirty, and return home at seven. Tomorrow's ten o'clock appointment is a grain inspection at the mill.
